name: ChainConnect
rootCause: ChainConnect bridge exploited on July 26. Attacker held ~329 ETH for ransom; whitehat agreement reached: attacker returned 280 ETH (85% of total stolen) to 0x840B3De19e3FAB72fa9A168bD8Dd71B678c57989 and retained ~49 ETH (15%) as bounty. Recovery confirmed July 31, 2026. descriptions.text: ChainConnect bridge exploited on July 26. Attacker held ~329 ETH for ransom; whitehat agreement reached: attacker returned 280 ETH (85% of total stolen) to 0x840B3De19e3FAB72fa9A168bD8Dd71B678c57989 and retained ~49 ETH (15%) as bounty. Recovery confirmed July 31, 2026. Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0xa6df21e27c5228af87e35122b506751c642fe012b2f61c84e046625718d0c85b Source: https://twitter.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2083213179333534148

ChainConnect’s EVM integration was compromised through unauthorized access. Approximately $650,000 in tokens was drained from the bridge contracts across Ethereum, BNB Chain, Avalanche C-Chain and Polygon in 23 transactions; bridge operations were paused immediately.

ChainConnect suffered an exploit on July 26, 2026, due to a missing sender-verification check in its Alien Proxy callback, enabling an unauthorized attacker to mint unbacked tokens and bridge them to EVM chains. About $650,000 was drained, but ~82.9% (~$615,000) was returned, with the remainder kept as a whitehat bounty. Missing sender-verification in the ProxyMultiVaultAlien_V10.onCheckAccumulatedFee callback allowed unauthorized minting and bridging of unbacked Alien TIP-3 tokens.
